data.text:
**Summary of findings**

Timeline from `/var/db/wan-watchdog/`:
- **02:01:44** modem log: `No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out` → modem lost upstream ranging with the ISP plant; metrics show `NOT_SYNCHRONIZED`.
- **02:14:10** modem log: `TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND` during re-registration.
- **02:28:21** modem log: `Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete`; metrics at 02:29 and 02:40 show `OPERATIONAL` (SNR ~37.6–37.9 dB).
- Watchdog decisions: `modem_not_operational` (02:06) → `modem_settling` (02:29) → **`reload`, reason `modem_operational` (02:30)**, plus a retry at 02:40. State shows 2 reloads already attempted in this outage, still down.

Firewall side:
- `ifconfig vtnet0`: WAN is `UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP`, active, address 198.51.100.27.
- `netstat -rn`: default route present via 198.51.100.1.
- `arp -a`: gateway 198.51.100.1 resolves (`00:17:10:9a:a3:96`) — L2 to the modem/CPE is fine.
- `ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1`: **100% packet loss** — traffic dies right at the ISP boundary even though the modem now reports registered/operational.
- `/var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0`: lease predates the modem's re-registration (renew not due until 2026/3/5), so the firewall is still carrying the pre-reboot WAN addressing/session against a modem that has since re-provisioned and re-registered.

data.reason: The internet dropped when the cable modem lost upstream ranging (T3 timeout) and later self-rebooted/re-registered, but the firewall is still using its pre-reboot WAN lease and session, so traffic is black-holed at the ISP boundary; the WAN needs to be reconfigured/renewed now that the modem is operational.

data.cause: The internet dropped when the cable modem lost upstream ranging (T3 timeout) and later self-rebooted/re-registered, but the firewall is still using its pre-reboot WAN lease and session, so traffic is black-holed at the ISP boundary; the WAN needs to be reconfigured/renewed now that the modem is operational.
evidence: Modem log: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44, matching outage start ~02:01 (cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl)
Modem log: 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' 02:14:10 then 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' 02:28:21 (modem-events.jsonl)
Modem metrics: status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, then OPERATIONAL at 02:29 and 02:40 with healthy SNR 37.6-37.9 dB (tail modem-metrics.jsonl)
Watchdog decided action 'reload', reason 'modem_operational' at 02:30 and a retry at 02:40; state.json shows 2 reloads in this outage (events.jsonl, state.json)
WAN interface vtnet0 is UP/RUNNING/LOWER_UP, active, 198.51.100.27 (ifconfig vtnet0); default route via 198.51.100.1 present (netstat -rn)
Gateway 198.51.100.1 has a resolved ARP entry on vtnet0, so L2 to the modem is fine (arp -a)
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 -> 100% packet loss: traffic dies at the ISP boundary despite modem being registered
dhclient lease for vtnet0 predates the modem re-registration (renew due 2026/3/5), i.e. stale WAN addressing (cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0)
data.recommendation: Reconfigure/renew the WAN interface on gw.lan so it re-runs DHCP and re-establishes its session with the now-registered modem (wan_reload). The watchdog itself flagged 'reload' once the modem became operational. If connectivity does not return after the renewal, escalate to the ISP, since the outage originated from upstream ranging loss/TFTP provisioning failure on their plant.
data.detail: Stale WAN DHCP lease/session after the modem re-registered
